title: Reliance interest and opportunities forgone
summary: The reliance interest concerns losses caused by changing position in reliance on a promise or agreement, measured against the position without that reliance.
notes:
Expenditures can count, but reliance is not confined to cash already paid. D&G Stout concerns a foregone sale opportunity, while Sullivan considers expenses and physical or emotional injury associated with surgery. Promissory estoppel is a possible basis of liability; reliance is a possible measure of recovery. A claim’s doctrinal basis does not by itself settle the measure or permit double recovery of the same loss.

The comparison is with the position before the induced change, including provable opportunities forgone. Reliance is both an interest relevant to remedy and a component of promissory estoppel, but those functions must be kept separate. A claimant must connect the change to the assurance. In D&G Stout, the lost opportunity to sell on favorable terms differs from hoped-for future distributorship profits. Hayes asks whether a retirement decision already made before the pension promise can count as induced reliance.
